text:
alex_r: FYI found an old plaintext AWS secret baked into a CI artifact (docker layer) from a staging build last week. Artifact is in our internal registry `artifacts.staging.redwood` and points to user `backup-ci`. Not public but needs rotation and a scan for other images.

tara: Oof. Is it an IAM user key or role creds? Any evidence it was used externally?

alex_r: It's an IAM access key (AKIA...). No external egress in cloudtrail for that key after the build time, but it's still active. The artifact sha is sha256:4f8b... and I can pull it to inspect layers.

kevin_h: Immediate plan: 1) Revoke the key in AWS, 2) Issue new key for the CI pipeline using short-lived role via OIDC (preferred), 3) Replace hardcoded value in image build, 4) Rebuild image and push, 5) Run image-scan to confirm no creds remain. Who will do AWS revoke?

alex_r: I'll revoke the key now and open a SEC ticket. Before revoking, I'll snapshot the artifact and store it in secure bucket for forensic.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Snapshotting artifact sha256:4f8b... to gs://sec-forensics/artifacts/4990012345/. ETA ~1m.

tara: Long term: migrate CI to assume-role via OpenID Connect so no long-lived keys are ever in images. Also add a pre-publish layer-scan (rg 'AKIA' + high-entropy check) in the CI pipeline.

kevin_h: Agreed. For immediate PR: add `aws sts assume-role` step that writes credentials to ephemeral env and ensure `.dockerignore` strips build-time creds. I'll draft the pipeline change.

alex_r: Revoked key at 11:02Z. No signs of key usage after build time. Ticket SEC-1512 created.

tara: Two KMS questions: 1) Should we rewrap any Vault-wrapped blobs touched by that key? 2) If images were built with plaintext creds, were any Vault unwrap events triggered by that key during build (unlikely, but check audit logs).

kevin_h: If the key was only used as a raw AWS access key (not for decrypting Vault data) we don't need to rewrap our KMS keys. But check Vault audit logs for unseal/unwrapping events around the build timestamp. If any unwraps correlating to build agent identity, rewrap or rotate transit key.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Scanning Vault audit for session origins matching `ci-builder-*` at 2026-03-22T10:00:00Z..2026-03-22T12:00:00Z. Found no unwraps with that access key.

tara: Good. RBAC follow-up: the build cluster role binding allowed `secrets:read` across namespace `*` historically for the build-sa. We're going to tighten that to only `secrets:get` for specific paths and add a policy that prevents writing credentials into images (scan fail).

kevin_h: I'll prepare a clusterrole -> role migration and smoke-tests. After rollout, run `kubectl auth can-i get secret --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:build-sa -n staging` which should be no by default except for the allowed prefix.

alex_r: For audit logging and detection: enable image registry audit hooks and add an alert on publishing if redact-scan fails. Also extend Vault audit retention to 180 days for builds.

sec-bot: sec-bot: Added registry publish hook that triggers a secret-detection job (uses yara + regex). Created alert rule SEC-REG-IMAGE-CRED with severity=high.

tara: Also ping infra to rotate any ephemeral KMS data keys used by image builders if they leverage envelope encryption in registry; but don't rotate the master key unless we see unwraps.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Noted. Creating infra ticket INF-778 to add OIDC provider and role mapping for CI.

kevin_h: Quick commands for rotation/remediation I used: 
```
# revoke key
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AAAAOLD --status Inactive --user-name backup-ci
aws iam delete-access-key --access-key-id AAAAOLD --user-name backup-ci
# assume-role example for pipeline
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-build-role --role-session-name ci-build-$(date +%s)
```

alex_r: Rebuild of offending image started with sanitized pipeline. Running post-push scan now.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Post-push layer-scan returned no secrets. Artifact replaced and old artifact tagged `quarantine/4990012345`.

tara: Nice. Follow-ups: 1) enforce pre-publish scan in CI (kevin), 2) migrate build-SA to OIDC role (infra/ops-bot), 3) audit all images in staging for `AKIA` patterns (alex). I'll own the checklist and postmortem.

sec-bot: sec-bot: Completed image-wide grep across staging registry, no other images with AKIA pattern found. Locking thread in 48h if no more findings. :lock:
